To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the isospin dependent quantum molecular dynamics (IDQMD) model can describe the experimental data of the mass distribution of the intermediate mass fragments (IMFs) and other fragments in the reactions of 197Au79 +12C6,197Au79 +26Al13,197Au79+ 63Cu29 and197Au79 +208Pb82 at 600 MeV per nucleon.

(i) the mass dependence is observed for the production of intermediate fragments, (ii) the isospin dependent model is found to reproduce the data well, (iii) the reduced isospin cross section and SACA are found to be more suitable for the study of heavy ion collisions.

1) The isospin dependent nucleon-nucleon cross section is important to study the heavy ion collisions and it is found that the reduced isospin dependence of NN cross section gives good results for low and intermediate Z fragment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production and the emission of fragments in heavy ion reactions.
the study of the fragment production mechanism using isospin-dependent quantum molecular dynamics.
the investigation of the production mechanism of intermediate mass fragments in the set of reactions 197Au+12C6 to 197Au+208Pb at 600 MeV per nucleon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the isospin dependent quantum molecular dynamics (IDQMD) model is able to describe the fragment production mechanism for the heavy systems in a wide range of impact parameter.
the isospin dependent quantum molecular dynamics (IDQMD) model can describe the experimental data of heavy ion collisions with a reasonable accuracy.
the mass dependence of IMF multiplicity is not only due to the mass effect but is also due to the density and the isospin effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the present work is an extension of our earlier work.
the isospin dependent quantum molecular dynamics model is a good tool for studying heavy ion collisions.
the isospin dependent cross section and SACA are very useful in describing the heavy ion collision at high energy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, we have successfully simulated the heavy ion collisions at an energy 400, 600 and 1000 MeV/nucleton using isospin independent QMD model.
the isospin dependent potential is very important for the study of fragment production mechanism in heavy ion collisions.
the isospin dependent cross section and the SACA algorithm are very useful in studying the fragmentation of the heavy ion collision.
